title: Silicon simulations found opposite temperature trends across harmonic orders
summary: Simulations of bulk silicon from 100 to 300 K predicted stronger third and fifth optical harmonics at higher temperatures and weaker ninth and higher harmonics. The calculations linked the lower-order increase to stronger local orbital coupling and the higher-order decrease to thermally induced disorder.
ai_technology: DeePTB learned tight-binding Hamiltonians; NEP89 learned interatomic potential
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: A 216-atom simulation sampled five configurations per temperature. The authors checked smaller-cell electronic structure and spectra against prior calculations and compared thermal trends qualitatively with published experiments.
evidence.unknown: The trends and proposed mechanisms come from modeled thermal configurations and a specific optical excitation. The study performed no new optical measurements.
evidence.ai_role: NEP89 generated thermal configurations in molecular dynamics; DeePTB estimated their electronic Hamiltonians, which were used to calculate the optical spectra.
